newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EDMONTON ROARS BACK TO BEAT DALLAS IN OVERTIME.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EDMONTON ROARS BACK TO BEAT DALLAS IN OVERTIME.

text.p: Kelly Buchberger scored at 9:15 of overtime, completing one of the greatest comebacks in playoff history, as the Edmonton Oilers rallied for a 4-3 victory over the Dallas Stars and a 2-1 lead in their Western Conference quarterfinal series on Sunday.
Edmonton, hosting its first playoff game in nearly five years, scored three goals in the final four minutes of regulation to force overtime.

The Oilers won it when Buchberger took a drop pass from Mats Lindgren, skated to the top of the right faceoff circle and let go a wrist shot that went through the legs of defenceman Darryl Sydor and beat former Edmonton goaltender Andy Moog to the glove side.
Curtis Joseph, coming off Friday's 4-0 victory, stopped 39 shots for the Oilers, who host Game Four of the best-of-seven series on Tuesday.

In Chicago, Sergei Krivokrasov did it to the Colorado Avalanche again in the playoffs, scoring at 11:03 of double overtime to give the Chicago Blackhawks a much-needed 4-3 victory in Game Three of their Western Conference series.

Krivokrasov, whose overtime goal won Game Three of last year's opening-round series against Colorado, skated out of a scramble along the left boards, cut to the net and lifted a shot just under the crossbar to breathe life into the Blackhawks.
"Patrick goes down a lot of times and I knew what I was going to do before I shot the puck," Krivokrasov said. "I saw him diving so I just shot the puck over his shoulder."
Eric Daze scored twice for Chicago.
Claude Lemieux, whose late goal forced overtime, also had an assist for the Avalanche.
At Florida, the New York Rangers in the lone Eastern Conference playoff game on Sunday evened their quarterfinal series with the Florida Panthers with a 3-0 victory.
Mike Richter made 31 saves for his seventh career playoff shutout and first in nearly three years. Wayne Gretzky had a goal and an assist.
The series, which is tied, 1-1, moves to New York for Game Three on Tuesday, with Game Four the following night.

"There's just some things you can't do against some teams and we were doing a lot of those things against Florida," Rangers coach Colin Campbell said. "You can't let them out-patience you. They can play a nothing-nothing tie into five overtimes if you let them."

In Anaheim, Darrin Shannon scored twice in the first 8:50 of the first period and Nikolai Khabibulin made 30 saves, leading the Phoenix Coyotes to a 4-1 victory over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim in Game Three of their Western Conference quarterfinal series.
Keith Tkachuk scored his team-leading third goal of the series, Mike Gartner also tallied and Cliff Ronning had three assists for the Coyotes, who trail the best-of-seven series, 2-1.
"The playoffs is about playing hard," Coyotes coach Don Hay said. "We thought we played hard in Anaheim, but it wasn't hard enough."
Phoenix hosts Game Four Tuesday.
Paul Kariya netted the lone goal for Anaheim, his third of the series. Defenceman J.J. Daigneault drew an assist, giving him six points in the first three games.

In St Louis, Steve Yzerman scored on a deflection with 4:38 left in the second period and the Detroit Red Wings ended a long power-play drought in a 3-2 victory over the Blues that gave them a 2-1 lead in their Western Conference quarterfinal series.

Yzerman's goal was one of Detroit's two power-play tallies in the second period. The Red Wings had been 0-for-17 in the series and scoreless in their last 30 power plays against St. Louis, dating back to the regular season.
Mike Vernon made 24 saves for Detroit, which reclaimed the home-ice advantage it lost in a 2-0 defeat in Game One.
Game Four of the best-of-seven series is Tuesday in St. Louis.

"Our composure is what we've got to work on, we can't get cocky," Red Wings coach Scotty Bowman said. "The retaliatory penalties are what you've got to watch for. You have to play with emotion, but it's hard to control. It's easy to say, hard to do."
Brett Hull had a goal and an assist for the Blues, who could not get the tying goal despite firing 15 shots at Vernon.
